pp:ee:2005:q10.title: GATE EE 2005 | Set 1 | Question: 10
pp:ee:2005:q10.question: If P and Q are two random events, then the following is TRUE
options: Independence of P and Q implies that probability (P$\cap$Q)=0
If P and Q are mutually exclusive, then they must be independent

detailed_solution.markdown:
(A) is false since of P and Q are independent

$Pr(P\cap Q)=Pr(P) \times Pr(Q)$

which need not be zero.

(B) is false since

$Pr(P\cup Q)=Pr(P) + Pr(Q)-Pr(P\cap Q)$

$\therefore \; Pr(P\cup Q)\leq Pr(P) + Pr(Q)$

(C) is false since independence and mutually exclusion are unrelated properties.

(D) is true

$$\begin{aligned} \text{since } P\cap Q&\subseteq P \\ \Rightarrow \;\; n(P\cap Q) &\leq n(P) \\ \Rightarrow \;\; Pr(P\cap Q) &\leq Pr(P) \end{aligned}$$

pp:ee:2005:q38.title: GATE EE 2005 | Set 1 | Question: 38
pp:ee:2005:q38.question: When subject to a unit step input, the closed loop control system shown in the figure will have a steady state error of

detailed_solution.concept: Control Systems - Mathematical Models of Physical Systems
detailed_solution.markdown: Using signal flow graph, Forward path gains $P_{1}=\left ( -1 \right )\times \frac{2}{s+2}=\frac{-2}{s+2}$ and $P_2=\frac{3}{s}\frac{2}{s+2}=\frac{6}{s(s+2)}$ Individual loop, $L_1=-1 \times \frac{3}{s}\times \frac{2}{s+2}=\frac{-6}{s(s+2)}$ Loop touches forward paths, therefore, $\Delta _1=1 \text{ and } \Delta _2=1$ $D=1-L_1 =1+\frac{6}{s(s+2)}=\frac{s(s+2)+6}{s(s+2)}$ Using Mason's gain formula, $\frac{Y(s)}{R(s)}=\frac{P_1\Delta _1+P_2\Delta _2}{\Delta } =\frac{-\frac{2}{s+2}\times 1+\frac{6}{s(s+2)}\times 1}{\frac{s(s+2)+6}{s(s+2)}}$ $\frac{Y(s)}{R(s)}=\frac{6-2s}{s^2+2s+6}$ For unit step input, $R(s)=\frac{1}{s}$ $$\begin{aligned} Y(s)&=R(s)\cdot \left ( \frac{6-2s}{s^2+2s+6} \right ) \\ Error&=E(s)=R(s)-Y(s) \\&=R(s)-R(s)\left (\frac{6-2s}{s^2+2s+6} \right ) \\ &=R(s)\left [ 1-\frac{6-2s}{s^2+2s+6} \right ]\\ E(s)&=\frac{1}{s}\left [ \frac{s^2+4s}{s^2+2s+6} \right ] \end{aligned}$$ Steady state value of error, using final value theoram, $$\begin{aligned}e_{ss}&=\lim_{s\rightarrow 0}sE(s) \\ &=\lim_{s\rightarrow 0}s\left [ \frac{1}{s}\cdot \frac{s^2+4s}{s^2+2s+6} \right ] \\ &=\lim_{s\rightarrow 0}\left [ \frac{s^2+4s}{s^2+2s+6} \right ]=0 \end{aligned}$$

pp:ee:2005:q41.title: GATE EE 2005 | Set 1 | Question: 41
pp:ee:2005:q41.question:
For the matrix
$$p=\begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2&2 \\ 0& -2 & 1\\ 0 &0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$$
one of the eigen values is equal to -2. Which of the following is an eigen vector ?

detailed_solution.markdown:
Since matrix is triangular, the eigen values are the diagonal elements themselves namely $\lambda =3, -2$ and 1.

Corresponding to eigen value $\lambda = -2$ let us find the eigen vector

$[A-\lambda I]\hat{x}=0$

$$\begin{bmatrix} 3-\lambda & -2 & 2\\ 0 & -2-\lambda & 1\\ 0& 0 & 1-\lambda \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$

Putting  $\lambda = -2$ in above equation we get,

$$\begin{bmatrix} 5 & -2 & 2\\ 0 & 0 & 1\\ 0& 0 & 3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$

Which gives the equations,

$$\begin{aligned} 5x_1-2x_2+2x_3&=0 \;\;...(i)\\ x_3 &=0 \;\;...(ii)\\ 3x_3&=0 \;\;...(iii) \end{aligned}$$

Since equation (ii) and (iii) are same we have

$$\begin{aligned} 5x_1-2x_2+2x_3&=0 \;\;...(i)\\ x_3 &=0 \;\;...(ii)\end{aligned}$$

Putting $x_2=k$, we get

$x_3=0, x_2=k$ and $5x_1-2k+2 \times 0=0$

$\Rightarrow \;x_1=2/5 \;k$

Eigen vectors are of the form

$$\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 2/5 k\\ k\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$

$$\begin{aligned} x_1:x_2:x_3&=2/5k:k:0\\ &=2/5:1:0\\ &=2:5:0 \end{aligned}$$

$$\therefore \;\;\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 2\\ 5\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$ is an eigen vector of matrix p.

$x =0$ or  $x=2$ are the stationary points.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Now, } f''(x) &= e^{-x}(2-2x)+(2x-x^2)(-e^{-x})\\ &= e^{-x}(2-2x-(2x-x^2))\\ &= e^{-x}(x^2-4x+2)\\ At\;x=0& \\ f''(0)&= e^{-0}(0-0+2)=2 \end{aligned}$$

Since $f''(x)=2$ is $\gt 0$ at $x=0$ we have a minima.

Now at $x=2$

$$\begin{aligned} f''(2)&=e^{-2}(2^2-4\times 2 +2) \\ &=-2e^{-2} \lt 0 \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore \;\; At \;\; x=2$ we have a maxima.

detailed_solution.concept: Electrical Machines - Three Phase Induction Machines
detailed_solution.markdown:
The resultant air-gap flux per pole is given by

$\phi _r=\frac{1}{4.44k_{\omega _1}N_{pn_1}}\left ( \frac{V}{f} \right )$

$\phi _r\propto \left ( \frac{V}{f} \right )$

Therefore, in order to avoid saturation in stator and rotor cores which would cause sharp increase in magnetization current, the flux $f_p$ must be kept constant. To achieve this, $\frac{V}{f}$ ratio must be kept constant.

Let, $V_0=$ Nominal voltage

$f_0=$ Nominal frequency

$X'_{20}=$ Nominal rotor standstill reactance reffered to stator then at any frequency f.

Then at any frequency f,

$$\begin{aligned} V &=\left ( \frac{f}{f_0} \right ) V_0\\ X'_2 &=\left ( \frac{f}{f_0} \right ) X'_{20} \\ \omega _s &=\left ( \frac{f}{f_0} \right )\omega _{20} \\ T_{max}&= \frac{3}{\left ( \frac{f}{f_0} \right )\omega _{s_0}}\left [ \frac{0.5 \left ( \frac{f}{f_0} \right )^2 V_0^2}{\left ( \frac{f}{f_0} \right )X'_{20}} \right ]\\ &= \frac{3}{\omega _{s_0}}\frac{0.5V_0^2}{X'_{20}}\\ &=\text{constant, independent of f} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ee:2005:q83.title: GATE EE 2005 | Set 1 | Question: 83
pp:ee:2005:q83.question:
A state variable system
$$\dot{X}\left ( t \right )=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1\\ 0 & -3 \end{bmatrix}X\left ( t \right )+ \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}u\left ( t \right )$$,
with the initial condition $$X\left ( 0 \right )=\begin{bmatrix} -1, &3 \end{bmatrix}^{T}$$ and the unit step input $u\left ( t \right )$ has

The state transition matrix

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\dot{x}(t)=\begin{bmatrix} 0 &-1 \\ 0& -3 \end{bmatrix}x(t)+\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}V(t) \;\;...(i)$$

$\dot{x}(t)=Ax(t)+Bu(t) \;\;...(ii)$

Comparing equation (i) and (ii), we get

$$A= \text{System  matrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0 &1 \\ 0 &-3 \end{bmatrix}$$ and $$B=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$

$$\begin{aligned}[sI-A]&=\begin{bmatrix} s &0 \\ 0 & s \end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix} 0 &1 \\ 0 &-3 \end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix} s &-1 \\ s &s+3 \end{bmatrix} \\ [sI-A]^{-1}&=\frac{\begin{bmatrix} s+3 &1 \\ 0 &s \end{bmatrix}}{s(s+3)-0x(-1)} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s} & \frac{1}{s(s+3)}\\ 0 &\frac{1}{s+3} \end{bmatrix} \\ [sI-A]^{-1}&=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s} & \frac{1}{3}\left ( \frac{1}{s}-\frac{1}{s+3} \right )\\ 0 &\frac{1}{s+3} \end{bmatrix} \\ &\text{State transition matrix } \\ &=L^{-1}[(sI-A)^{-1}]\\ \phi (t)&=\begin{bmatrix} 1 &\frac{1}{3}(1-e^{-3t}) \\ 0& e^{-3t} \end{bmatrix} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ee:2005:q84.title: GATE EE 2005 | Set 1 | Question: 84
pp:ee:2005:q84.question:
A state variable system
$$\dot{X}\left ( t \right )=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1\\ 0 & -3 \end{bmatrix}X\left ( t \right )+ \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}u\left ( t \right )$$,
with the initial condition $$X\left ( 0 \right )=\begin{bmatrix} -1, &3 \end{bmatrix}^{T}$$ and the unit step input $u\left ( t \right )$ has

the state transition equation

detailed_solution.markdown:
ZIR (zero Input Response) $=\phi (t) \times X(0)$

$$=\begin{bmatrix} 1 &\frac{}{3}(1-e^{-3t}) \\ 0& e^{-3t} \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} -1\\ 3 \end{bmatrix}$$

$$=\begin{bmatrix} -1+1-e^{-3t} \\ 3 e^{-3t} \end{bmatrix} =\begin{bmatrix} -e^{-3t} \\ 3 e^{-3t} \end{bmatrix}$$

ZSR (Zero State Response)

$=L^{-1}[(sI-A)^{-1}BU(s)]$

$$=L^{-1}\left \{ \begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s} & \frac{1}{s(s+3)}\\ 0& \frac{1}{s+3} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\frac{1}{s}\right \}$$

$$=l^{-1}\begin{bmatrix} 1/s^2\\ 0 \end{bmatrix} =\begin{bmatrix} t\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$

$\therefore$  State transition equation

$$\;\;\; =ZIR+ZSR=\begin{bmatrix} -e^{-3t} \\ 3 e^{-3t} \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} t\\0 \end{bmatrix}$$

$$\;\;\;=\begin{bmatrix} t-e^{-3t}\\ 3 e^{-3t} \end{bmatrix}$$
